subject: Multiple color scales in faceted graphs

messages.author: b4ce8db4b948fdbd
messages.subject: Multiple color scales in faceted graphs
parts:
I'm plotting different variables in a faceted graph, and the variables have different scales. Is it possible for each graph to have its own color scale? Using the code below, the color variation for most of the panels is uniform since one of the variable's data range (e.g., depth_r) is much broader than the others.

Here's a link to the data:
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/16369868/nav_gg.Rdata

Here is the code:
m <- ggplot(nav.gg,aes(lon_dd_r,lat_dd_r))
m + geom_point(aes(colour = value)) + facet_wrap(~variable)

Thanks,
Kevin

--
Kevin Stierhoff, PhD
Research Fisheries Biologist
NOAA Fisheries Service - Southwest Fisheries Science Center

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Multiple color scales in faceted graphs
parts:
Kevin,

Cool-looking data!

As far as I know--unless 0.9 has new capabilities in this
area--ggplot2 can't do what you want here. You have two options:
first, use viewport and set up multiple independent plots, each with
an independent color scale; second, rescale "value" so that they're
all in the same range, e.g.

nav.gg.rescaled <- ddply(nav.gg,.(variable),function(d){d$value <-
rescale(d$value); d})

and then plot exactly as before. This puts the data (subsetted by
variable) on a common 0-1 scale.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Multiple color scales in faceted graphs
parts:
Hey Kevin,


You need to load the 'scales' package if you are using ggplot2 v 0.9.

library(scales) which has the rescale function.

Best,
Art
